newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank lending fell 0.4 pct in December -- BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank lending fell 0.4 pct in December -- BOJ.

text.p: Aggregate outstanding lending by Japan's 149 banks dipped 0.4 percent in December from a year earlier to 533.27 trillion yen, the third month it has dropped on a year-on-year basis, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) said on Thursday.

The decline in lending reflected efforts by Japanese firms to cut borrowing, and the lending is likely to remain at low levels for a while due to slow demand for new loans from corporations and for housing loans from individuals, banking industry sources said.
The total outstanding lending by Japan's 10 big commercial banks, based on a daily average, was up 0.2 percent at 246.30 trillion yen in December, the BOJ said in a statement.
The total for three long-term credit banks fell 3.4 percent to 45.32 trillion yen and that for seven major trust banks was down 4.2 percent at 53.80 trillion yen.
The decline in December was marginally smaller than drops of 0.5 percent posted in both November and October, partly because of an increase in borrowings for winter bonus payments, the sources said.
